idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why Your Toilet Keeps Running: Flapper Seal Failure
description: When a toilet runs constantly, the issue usually sits inside the water tank. The flexible rubber flapper creates a seal over the flush valve drain seat. Over time, water treatment chemicals and mineral deposits cause the rubber to harden, warp, or deteriorate. Even a slight imperfection allows water to trickle constantly into the bowl, keeping the water level down and preventing the fill valve float from shutting off. Before replacing the entire fill valve assembly, check the flapper seal for stiffness, buildup, or improper chain tension. A quick flapper replacement often resolves the leak and prevents wasted water.

At the bottom of the tank, a dark rubber flapper valve rests over the flush valve orifice, showing a microscopic gap due to hardened, warped rubber material, with a subtle blue stream of water trickling past the seal into the drain throat below. No text, no visual annotations, no arrows, no logos, no fake branding, no watermarks.
visual_story: The visual uses an educational section view of the toilet tank interior to highlight the mechanical connection between the flapper valve and the flush seat. The viewer immediately notices the point of failure: a warped rubber flapper allowing a continuous trickle of water into the flush orifice, demonstrating why the water level stays low and forces the fill valve to remain open.

on_image_text.explanation: A degraded flapper fails to seal the tank drain, letting water leak into the bowl constantly.
on_image_text.takeaway: Inspect the rubber seal for damage before replacing the entire fill valve assembly.
